subject: community-medicine
title: Kangaroo Mother Care, Breastfeeding, and Levels of Newborn Care

steps.title: What kangaroo mother care is
steps.tx: **Kangaroo mother care** is continuous skin to skin contact between a low birth weight baby and the mother's chest, combined with exclusive breastfeeding and early discharge with close follow up. The baby wears only a cap, socks, and nappy, held upright and prone between the breasts under the mother's clothing. It was developed in Colombia for settings short of incubators and now has global evidence behind it.
steps.say: Kangaroo mother care keeps the small baby skin to skin on the mother's chest. Her body becomes the incubator, and breastfeeding completes the method.

steps.tx: **Kangaroo mother care** is continuous skin to skin contact for a low birth weight baby on the mother chest, together with exclusive breastfeeding and early discharge plus close follow up. The baby wears only a cap, socks, and a nappy, and lies upright and prone between the breasts beneath her clothes. The method began in Colombia where incubators were scarce, and later trials have supported it worldwide. Her chest supplies heat the machine would otherwise provide.
steps.say: The small baby stays upright and skin to skin on the mother chest, dressed only in a cap, socks, and nappy, with exclusive breastfeeding and early discharge. The practice started in Colombia as a substitute for scarce incubators.

steps.title: Which babies benefit and proven gains
steps.tx: Babies below two thousand grams who are haemodynamically stable gain most from **kangaroo care for low birth weight babies**: trials show lower mortality, less hypothermia, fewer severe infections, better weight gain, and longer exclusive breastfeeding. The method needs no electricity, which makes it decisive in district units and at home after discharge. Unstable babies first need stabilisation in a special newborn care unit.
steps.say: Stable babies under two thousand grams thrive with kangaroo care. It cuts deaths, cold stress, and infection while improving weight gain and breastfeeding.

steps.title: How long and how to position
steps.tx: Sessions should last as long as possible each day, ideally beyond eighteen hours, with the head turned to one side, neck slightly extended, hips flexed in a frog position, and the abdomen at the mother's epigastrium so her breathing stimulates the baby; this is the correct **kangaroo position for preterm babies**. Fathers and other family members can share skin to skin sessions so the mother rests without breaking continuity.
steps.say: Keep the baby skin to skin for most of the day. Head turned aside, hips flexed like a frog, and family members can take turns.

points: Head turned, airway open, neck extended
Hips flexed, arms flexed, frog posture

right.title: Dangerous errors
points: Baby wrapped over clothes, no skin contact
Neck flexed, chin on chest, airway blocked
Short feeds only sessions with long cold gaps

steps.tx: When a preterm baby cannot latch for long, the mother can hand express milk into a sterile cup so feeding continues alongside skin to skin care. In the **kangaroo position for preterm babies**, sessions ideally run beyond eighteen hours, with the head turned aside, the neck slightly extended, and the hips flexed like a frog against the mother's epigastrium. Fathers may take turns so rest does not break contact.

steps.title: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months
steps.tx: Only breast milk, not even water, for the first six months defines **exclusive breastfeeding**, which delivers sterile nutrition, secretory IgA (immunoglobulin A), lactoferrin, and living cells that no formula reproduces. Colostrum in the first days is concentrated antibody rich milk and must never be discarded. Feeding should start within the first hour of birth and continue on demand day and night, eight to twelve times daily.
steps.say: Exclusive breastfeeding means only breast milk for six months, starting within the first hour. Colostrum is the baby's first vaccine, never waste it.

rows: Coats gut and blocks pathogen attachment

steps.title: Feeding the low birth weight baby
steps.tx: Small babies who cannot yet suckle receive expressed breast milk by cup, spoon, or gastric tube every two to three hours, advancing volumes by birth weight charts; this graded approach is **feeding support for low birth weight babies**. Hind milk, richer in fat, speeds weight gain. Supplements of iron, vitamin D, calcium, and phosphorus follow unit protocols, and daily weighing catches faltering growth before illness declares itself.
steps.say: A baby too small to suck gets expressed breast milk by cup or tube every two to three hours. Daily weights show whether growth is on track.

nodes.label: Feed by cup or tube every 2 to 3 hours

steps.title: Thermal protection: the warm chain
steps.tx: Newborns lose heat by evaporation, conduction, convection, and radiation, so delivery rooms maintain the **warm chain for newborn care**: a warm room near twenty five degrees, immediate drying, skin to skin contact, warm resuscitation, and delayed bathing. Hypothermia below thirty six point five degrees raises oxygen consumption, hypoglycaemia, and sepsis risk, and it silently worsens every other neonatal illness.
steps.say: The warm chain starts with a warm room and instant drying. A cold baby burns sugar and oxygen faster and slides into sepsis more easily.

right.title: Warm chain answers
points: Dry at once, remove wet cloth
Warm surfaces and pre warmed towels
Close draughts, keep room near 25 degrees
Skin to skin and kangaroo care

steps.title: Organisation of newborn care levels
steps.tx: India grades newborn services so each baby reaches the right intensity: the newborn care corner in the labour room, the newborn stabilisation unit at block level, and the **special newborn care unit** at district hospital level with radiant warmers, oxygen, continuous positive airway pressure, and trained nurses round the clock. Referral transport must keep the baby warm, with kangaroo transport preferred when an ambulance warmer is absent.
steps.say: Care rises from the labour room corner to the block stabilisation unit and the district special care unit. Warm transport, ideally kangaroo style, links them.

rows: Resuscitation and warmth at every delivery point

Follow up of development after discharge

steps.title: Discharge criteria and follow up
steps.tx: A kangaroo baby goes home when feeding directly from the breast, gaining fifteen to twenty grams daily for three consecutive days, maintaining temperature in kangaroo care, and the mother is confident; these are the standard **kangaroo discharge criteria**. Follow up runs weekly until the baby reaches forty weeks post conception or two thousand five hundred grams, watching weight, feeding, immunisation, hearing, vision, and development.
steps.say: Discharge needs steady weight gain of fifteen to twenty grams a day and a confident mother. Weekly follow up continues until the baby reaches term weight.

steps.title: Counselling the family
steps.tx: Success at home depends on **kangaroo counselling for families**: demonstrate the position, let the mother practise under observation, teach hand washing, danger signs of poor feeding, fast breathing, chest indrawing, fever, cold body, and convulsions, and enrol the father and grandmother as supporters. Written instructions in the local language plus the ASHA worker's scheduled home visits keep the practice alive after discharge.
steps.say: Counsel the whole family, not just the mother. Everyone should know the position, hand washing, and the danger signs that mean rush back.
